findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 (breaking scripted contract)
findings.body: The exit code signalling "recreate upgrade required" was changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means "feature disabled". Since the documented purpose of this command is to be consumed by scripts/CI pipelines via the exit code, any existing automation keyed on exit code 4 will now interpret a disabled-feature error as "recreate needed" (or miss recreate signals entirely). This should at least be called out in release/upgrade notes, and any other consumers of the constant (e.g. the operator's update logic) verified.

findings.title: No assertion on the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the stderr text and does not assert the process exit code is 4 (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED). Since the exit-code contract is the documented machine-readable interface (and codes were just renumbered), a regression in the exit code would go undetected. Also no test covers the `check` subcommand with the feature disabled.
